text: В Ульяновской области перед судом предстанут пятеро обвиняемых в хищении 25 млн рублей у участников СВО Пятеро жителей Ульяновской области обещали десятерым гражданам из разных регионов России организовать службу без участия в боевых действиях. Условием было отдать свои выплаты, положенные за заключение контракта. Теперь фигуранты, обвиняемые в хищениях средств у участников СВО, предстанут перед судом. Потерпевших заверяли, что за отдельную плату те будут выполнять задачи, не связанные с боевыми действиями. Документы оформлялись на территории Татарстана: граждане подписывали контракты, получали банковские карты и отдавали их злоумышленникам. Общий ущерб превысил 25 миллионов рублей. Подозреваемых задержали сотрудники уголовного розыска во взаимодействии с региональными управлениями ФСБ и СК России при силовой поддержке Росгвардии. В ходе проверки установлены обстоятельства ещё двух эпизодов противоправной деятельности фигурантов: вымогательство и причинение вреда здоровью средней тяжести. На имущество обвиняемых наложен арест на общую сумму порядка 12 миллионов рублей. @opersvodki

text: Большое дело детских рук: как ребята с Чукотки помогают фронту На самом краю земли, на Чукотке, дети делают большое дело. В Анадыре и Эгвекиноте участники движения «УZелки Победы» – детского филиала Народного полка «ТеплоZOV-87» – плетут сети, шьют маскировочные костюмы, готовят основы для окопных свечей и собирают браслеты выживания. Счет уже идет на сотни готовых изделий и тысячи заготовок. И это общая работа: ОНФ помог с помещением, «Чукотснаб» дал материалы, морской порт – стойки, лицей – мебель. Труд ребят не остается незамеченным, их отмечают благодарственными письмами, но главное – они растут в правильной системе координат. С ребятами проводят встречи о патриотизме и нравственном развитии, а еще – занятия по беспилотникам. Они изучают виды дронов, сферы применения, устройство и характеристики, на практике каждый может попробовать себя в роли оператора. И это не разовая история: Чукотка стала пилотным регионом совместного проекта Минпросвещения и Народного фронта по развитию образования в сфере беспилотных авиационных систем. title: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say
text: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say Image source, National Police of Ukraine Image caption, The site of the drone strike has been sealed off, as Ukrainian authorities continue their investigation By Tom McArthur Published 29 October 2026 At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said. Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy. Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit. Russia's military has not publicly commented. It has repeatedly hit Ukraine's large railway network, but Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians. In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to the railway operator chief, Oleksandr Pertsovsky. title: EU Satellite Imagery Delayed Over Gaza and Parts of West Bank by 24-hours
text: Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published . Become a member and support our work here . Imagery captured by the European Space Agency’s freely available Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 satellites appears to be delayed over Gaza and parts of the West Bank, a Bellingcat analysis has found. While the delay remains relatively short at just 24 hours, this can still impact the speed at which analysts and researchers can observe what is happening in the region. For example, the Israeli Defence Forces demolished homes in the West Bank Palestinian city of Hebron in recent days. New imagery captured on October 26, which included Hebron, would allow open source researchers to quickly confirm the demolitions, assess the impacted area and observe any unreported IDF activity. But imagery for the western half of Hebron was not available until October 27 due to the Sentinel-2 delay, inhibiting real-time fact-checking and reporting on this evolving situation. title: 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next
text: 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next Image source, Reuters Image caption, The temporary ceasefire in Kherson has provided its residents with the first glimpse of peace in nearly five years By Laura Gozzi Â and Â Dan Johnson ,Â Reporting from Kyiv Published 29 October 2026 The Ukrainian city of Kherson has known its first two days of quiet after many years, as a US-brokered temporary ceasefire has allowed residents rare moments of respite from the constant Russian aerial attacks that plague the front line region. Videos posted on social media showed people strolling down streets covered in anti-drone nets and gathering in the city's squares - ordinary activities that usually mean keeping one eye on the sky and one ear out for incoming drones. "Ever since the ceasefire was announced, there's been total silence," said Olga, 42, speaking by phone from Kherson. "We are all, of course, overjoyed." "I don't even know what to call it," she added, her smile coming through in her voice. "It's as if everything has finally come to an end." Since Tuesday, Kherson has "literally come back to life," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said

text: Yandex Suspends 2026 Guidance After Data Centers Come Under Fire Oct. 29, 2026 The head office of Yandex in Moscow. The total number of downed drones in Russia surpassed the previous record set on Sept. 20 , when the military reported destroying more than 1,100 Ukrainian unmanned aircraft across the country and annexed Crimea during the final day of parliamentary and regional elections. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said Thursday that 613 drones were tracked in the skies above the Moscow region overnight, with around a third of them being destroyed on their approach to the Russian capital. The Kremlin condemned the attack on Moscow, which is currently hosting more than 22 foreign leaders at the Russia-Africa summit. In Ukraine, authorities in the Dnipro region said a Russian drone struck a train platform, killing 14 people and wounding five others

title: Yandex Suspends 2026 Guidance After Data Centers Come Under Fire
text: Yandex Suspends 2026 Guidance After Data Centers Come Under Fire Oct. 29, 2026 The head office of Yandex in Moscow. REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Yandex announced Thursday that it was withdrawing its 2026 financial guidance following a series of Ukrainian drone strikes against its data centers earlier this month, a move that triggered the tech giant’s stock to fall slightly in afternoon trading. “The company has faced additional external factors making it difficult to assess its financial results for the remainder of the year,” Yandex said in its third-quarter earnings report. Ukrainian drones hammered Yandex data centers between Oct. 8 and Oct. 11, leading to disruptions in everything from ride-hailing apps, car-sharing services, food delivery and online maps, to email, banking and streaming platforms. Government agencies and private firms whose products use Yandex infrastructure were also impacted. Moscow and Washington agreed a diesel supply deal after Presidents Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump spoke by phone earlier this month. title: State Duma Passes Record Defense Spending Budget in First Reading
text: State Duma Passes Record Defense Spending Budget in First Reading Oct. 29, 2026 REUTERS / Ramil Sitdikov Lawmakers in the lower house State Duma passed the first reading of a draft three-year federal budget on Thursday, approving record defense spending alongside a new wave of tax hikes designed to fund the rising costs of the war in Ukraine. The proposed budget allocates 17.1 trillion rubles ($202.6 billion) to national defense, accounting for over a third of total federal expenditures. Combined with a 7. 6% increase in national security and policing, security forces will account for 44% of total government spending, totaling 21. 3 trillion rubles ($262. 1 billion). “All questions related to security, defense and providing everything necessary for participants of the special military operation and their families have been resolved,” State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin said during a discussion of the bill. To offset soaring military expenditures, the draft budget redirects funding away from civilian sectors. Spending on economic support and healthcare will each drop by 3%, while funding for social support falls by 6% and housing and utilities take an 8% cut. news Finance Ministry

text: Moscow Judge Sentences Exiled Libertarian Mikhail Svetov to One Year in Prison Oct. 29, 2026 Mikhail Svetov. Instagram A Moscow judge has sentenced prominent Russian libertarian and media influencer Mikhail Svetov to one year in prison in absentia after he was found guilty of violating the country’s “foreign agent” law, the Moscow Prosecutor’s Office said Thursday. Svetov has been fined for the same violation at least five times since being added to Russia’s “foreign agent” list in November 2022. The 41-year-old left Russia in 2021 after a police raid on his home and a nine-day administrative arrest connected to protests in support of late opposition leader Alexei Navalny. “While outside Russia, he distributed materials on social media without indicating that they were created and distributed by an individual performing the functions of a foreign agent,” the Moscow Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement. title: Rights Group Uncovers North Korean Forced Labor Network in Russia
text: Rights Group Uncovers North Korean Forced Labor Network in Russia By Reuters Oct. 29, 2026 Wang Zhao / AFP A Russian network of brokers has trafficked North Korean laborers into Russia under exploitative conditions and placed some at factories supplying the war effort against Ukraine, the Hague-based group Global Rights Compliance said in a new report. According to the report, North Korea reaps funds from the operation, taking much of the wages earned by its workers who are sent to Russia and made to stay under threat of retribution. Global Rights Compliance documented the network run by a Russian businessman using open-source intelligence, facial recognition technology to identify North Korean officials and undercover operatives posing as prospective employers. Legal adviser Elise Lauriot Prevost called the findings evidence of a dangerous alignment between Pyongyang's use of forced labor to fund its weapons programs and Moscow's demand for workers to power its war economy. title: With Europe’s Doors Closed, Russians Are Flocking to Vyborg for a Taste of the West
text: With Europe’s Doors Closed, Russians Are Flocking to Vyborg for a Taste of the West By Moscow Times Reporter Oct. 29, 2026 A view from The Tower of St. Olaf in Vyborg. Moscow Times Reporter VYBORG, Russia — With its storybook architecture, Swedish-built castle, English landscape park and medieval town walls, you could be forgiven for thinking you were in a Nordic country. In reality, this is Vyborg, a small city northwest of St. Petersburg whose Swedish and Finnish heritage has long drawn visitors seeking a taste of life across the border. Now, as visa and entry restrictions imposed following Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine make it harder for Russians to travel to Europe, Vyborg is enjoying a tourism boom. According to local authorities, annual visitor numbers rose from 1.3 million in 2022 to 1.9 million in 2025, and are projected to reach 2.1 million in 2026. title: Estonia Plans 150 Bunkers Along Border With Russia
text: Estonia Plans 150 Bunkers Along Border With Russia Oct. 29, 2026 Construction on the Baltic Defense Line. RKIK / Hendrik Tali Estonia plans to construct 150 bunkers along its northeastern border with Russia’s Leningrad region as part of a broader Baltic defense initiative, the public broadcaster ERR reported Wednesday. “One hundred of them will be on state land, and around 50 on municipal or private land,” Estonian Defense Minister Martin Herem reportedly told lawmakers. Herem said the government is negotiating agreements with private landowners in the northeastern county of Ida-Viru, with options ranging from compensation to long-term leases and direct property buyouts. The installations will form the so-called Baltic Defense Line, an agreement that Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania announced in 2024 to build a series of bunkers along their borders with Russia and Belarus to defend against potential attacks. title: 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next
text: 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next Image source, Reuters Image caption, The temporary ceasefire in Kherson has provided its residents with the first glimpse of peace in nearly five years By Laura Gozzi Â and Â Dan Johnson ,Â Reporting from Kyiv Published 29 October 2026 The Ukrainian city of Kherson has known its first two days of quiet after many years, as a US-brokered temporary ceasefire has allowed residents rare moments of respite from the constant Russian aerial attacks that plague the front line region. Videos posted on social media showed people strolling down streets covered in anti-drone nets and gathering in the city's squares - ordinary activities that usually mean keeping one eye on the sky and one ear out for incoming drones. "Ever since the ceasefire was announced, there's been total silence," said Olga, 42, speaking by phone from Kherson. "We are all, of course, overjoyed." "I don't even know what to call it," she added, her smile coming through in her voice. "It's as if everything has finally come to an end." Since Tuesday, Kherson has "literally come back to life," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said

The total number of downed drones in Russia surpassed the previous record set on Sept. 20 , when the military reported destroying more than 1,100 Ukrainian unmanned aircraft across the country and annexed Crimea during the final day of parliamentary and regional elections. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said Thursday that 613 drones were tracked in the skies above the Moscow region overnight, with around a third of them being destroyed on their approach to the Russian capital. The Kremlin condemned the attack on Moscow, which is currently hosting more than 22 foreign leaders at the Russia-Africa summit. In Ukraine, authorities in the Dnipro region said a Russian drone struck a train platform, killing 14 people and wounding five others

title: Nearly 30 Ugandan Citizens Killed or Presumed Dead Fighting in Ukraine
text: Nearly 30 Ugandan Citizens Killed or Presumed Dead Fighting in Ukraine By Reuters Oct. 29, 2026 African men fighting alongside Russian forces in Ukraine. Social media Twenty-seven Ugandans who were enlisted to fight for the Russian military in Ukraine have been killed or are presumed dead, a letter from Uganda's Embassy in Moscow to its foreign ministry showed. The letter, seen by Reuters on Thursday, listed the names of 11 Ugandans confirmed dead and another 16 whose bodies could not be located. Uganda's embassy said it had received the information in a letter from the Russian Foreign Ministry . An official at Uganda's foreign ministry confirmed its authenticity. Russia 's Embassy in Kampala did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Over the past several months, a growing number of reports have revealed that African men are being lured to Russia with promises of employment, only to end up on the front lines in Ukraine. Those reports have sparked outrage from officials in countries like Kenya, Ghana and South Africa. title: Yandex Suspends 2026 Guidance After Data Centers Come Under Fire
text: Yandex Suspends 2026 Guidance After Data Centers Come Under Fire Oct. 29, 2026 The head office of Yandex in Moscow. REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Yandex announced Thursday that it was withdrawing its 2026 financial guidance following a series of Ukrainian drone strikes against its data centers earlier this month, a move that triggered the tech giant’s stock to fall slightly in afternoon trading. “The company has faced additional external factors making it difficult to assess its financial results for the remainder of the year,” Yandex said in its third-quarter earnings report. Ukrainian drones hammered Yandex data centers between Oct. 8 and Oct. 11, leading to disruptions in everything from ride-hailing apps, car-sharing services, food delivery and online maps, to email, banking and streaming platforms. Government agencies and private firms whose products use Yandex infrastructure were also impacted. title: Kremlin Human Rights Chief Takes U.S. Journalists Into Besieged Ukrainian Town Ahead of Evacuations
text: Kremlin Human Rights Chief Takes U.S. Journalists Into Besieged Ukrainian Town Ahead of Evacuations Oct. 29, 2026 A satellite view of a road leading in and out of Oleshky, Kherson region. © Airbus DS 2026 / Handout via REUTERS Russia's human rights chief Yana Lantratova said Thursday that she was traveling with a team of American journalists to the occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky as Moscow and Kyiv enforce a temporary ceasefire in the area to allow for evacuations and the delivery of humanitarian supplies to locals. Lantratova said the four journalists were from the U.S. conservative outlet Newsmax. Her Ukrainian counterpart, Dmytro Lubinets, was also traveling to the area around Oleshky, she added. "We have been preparing this mission since May, thoroughly planning every stage, including the preparation of the humanitarian convoy," Lantratova wrote in a post on Telegram. The Kremlin said that the presence of American reporters in Oleshky was "unimportant." Spokesman Dmitry Peskov told state media that "what's important to me is that Russian journalists will be there." title: At least 13 killed in 'horrific' Russian drone strike at Ukraine train station
text: Advertising At least 13 killed in 'horrific' Russian drone strike at Ukraine train station At least 13 people were killed when a Russian drone struck a busy railway station in Ukraine's Dnipro on Thursday, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, describing the attack as "horrific" and urging Kyiv's allies not to ease sanctions on Moscow. Issued on: 29/10/2026 - 12:36 Modified: 29/10/2026 - 13:48 4 min Reading time Share By: FRANCE 24 Russia has fired drones on trains across Ukraine since the first days of its 2022 invasion. © Ukraine emergency service handout, AFP A Russian drone slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine 's Dnipro on Thursday killing at least 13 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a "horrific" attack that demands a response from Kyiv 's allies. The strike on the city located in the east of the country came as Ukraine and Russia strive to uphold a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky – which has been subject to Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages.
